classes.title: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
Cain was born first, just like Esau. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground”, a man of the field, which already tells you what is going on. “And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Cain already knew right from wrong, because his father taught him animal sacrifice, but over a process of time Cain turned evil and did not do what the Lord commanded.

Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:” “But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance fell because he was corrected. What really started all of this? Correction.

Solomon says, “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way”. Cain had forsaken the way over a process of time, so the correction was grievous to him. That grievous spirit nourished bitterness, and the bitterness grew until he murdered his brother. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with a bitter spirit.

Then: “and he that hateth reproof shall die”, because the wages of sin is death. Paul says, “For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.” If we judged ourselves we would not have to be told about the bitterness, envy, hatred and malice inside us; when we refuse, the Lord has to bring the chastening. Cain refused to get himself right, and he became the father of wickedness.

precepts.label: Proverbs 13:10
precepts.why:
Bitterness does not travel alone. Envy, pride, hatred and evil suspicion come bundled together like a cable TV package. Solomon names one: “Only by pride cometh contention”.

Cain was contending because pride was on him. Cain's attitude was: I am not going to make it right with my brother; my brother is the one who is off; in fact, I have to put him to death, because he is making me look bad. That is pride. Cain did not want to take the correction.

Then: “but with the well advised is wisdom.” The well advised are the ones who do well, like Abel. Wisdom says, let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother. When correction comes, pride contends with it, while wisdom takes it and makes things right with the brother.

precepts.label: James 3:16
precepts.why:
“For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” Genesis 4 is an account of envying and strife. Cain was not doing right, he saw Abel doing right, and that built envy, the same spirit that shows up later between Esau and Jacob. It was there from the beginning.

Then comes confusion. All of a sudden Cain did not know right from wrong, and every evil work followed: he slew his brother. When you are confused, saying, I do not know where this is coming from, every evil work will be the result.

Confusion is Satan's playground. Satan loves us operating in confusion. That is why his children throw every kind of confusion into the media and everywhere they go, and why leaders of other nations have said they do not want that American media in their countries. They know every evil work hides behind that cloud of confusion.

precepts.label: Galatians 5:26
precepts.why:
“Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.” Cain wanted to be the man; that is vain glory.

Provoking one another means agitating a brother to play him out of position, because you are envious of him. You do something to provoke him to evil so you can justify your position against him.

We see this even in marriage. A brother provokes his wife, she leaves the house and does something foolish, and he sits back saying, I told you the sister was off, I told you she was evil. No, brother: you are the evil one, you provoked your wife. We are not going for that foolishness here. Envy provokes, and provoking is how the bitter spirit sets up its victim.

precepts.label: Romans 7:11
precepts.why:
What is bitterness? It is sin. “For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.” Taking occasion by the commandment means you can only recognize sin through the commandments of God. How do you know you are in the middle of sin? The law says you shall not hate your brother in your heart, and when you meditate on it you realize, I have an evil spirit toward that brother. The law brings it to the surface.

Sin “deceived me”: you did not know bitterness was a sin, because you were deceived. But the law gives clarity. Like fog lights, it pierces the cloud of confusion. That is why the law is called a light: so you can see through the nonsense your mind was thinking.

Then sin “by it slew me.” When the scripture comes out, you feel cut, because you are no longer deceived and can see clearly. What you see on the other side of the fog is yourself in the mirror of the Bible, realizing how evil you were. Some people do not like the light and love to walk in darkness, saying, do not call that out, that is not me; brothers wearing purple and gold, a ribbon of blue and fringes, who are only blue ribbon Christians. We do not want to be those night walkers.

precepts.label: Psalms 37:8
precepts.why:
“Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.” That bitterness is the spirit of Cain, and in that wrath you might slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray one. None of us is above this. Do not sit in the congregation thinking so-and-so is getting cut with the scriptures; brother, that is you. Every lesson the leadership brings out is for us. The moment you think, I am not dealing with that, Satan already has you lined up and counts you on his team.

Go back to Genesis 4:8: “And Cain talked with Abel his brother”. This is the deception. Cain acted like his friend, talking with him over time about his flocks, until he could lure him out to the field: “when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” Solomon describes that man: “He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;” “When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.” Murder, envy, pride and covetousness are all in there. “Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.” That is why it is called a root of bitterness: roots are covered by soil where nobody can see them, but the Lord always brings it to the surface. “Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein”, and “a flattering mouth worketh ruin.”

John names the spirit: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures, and he came back as Esau. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead; carry an evil eye toward your brother and you are in the same spirit. “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death.” “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer”. And Sirach warns, “When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” Brothers say, the white man is the devil, they are going to be destroyed, they are going into captivity, and then carry hatred toward their own brother, moving in the same spirit.

“Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.” Bitterness is a progression: it starts with a correction or an offense, then pride comes in and you will not speak to the brother, then when you do speak it is in deceit, masking envy, anger and hatred, and in the end it destroys you and those around you. “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump”: a little bitterness defiles the whole soul. Christ said, “Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed”. Leaven looks flat at first and grows as it bakes, so do not let the hate bake. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God before it festers and overcomes you.

precepts.label: Genesis 33:4
precepts.why:
“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” That is the bitterness, and it plans over a process of time. It is the same thing we read in Genesis 4: Cain slew Abel, and Esau wanted to kill Jacob. Cain was the firstborn and Esau was the firstborn. Same spirit.

To see how someone can hold bitterness, hatred and malice toward you and hide it completely, look at Genesis 33, long after Esau said he hated his brother: “And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.” Someone who hates you can play the long game. He can pretend to be your friend and on your side while he waits for the moment to hit you at your worst. They call them liberals today. That's the liberal for you: oh, we love you niggers, I mean black people. Jacob knew Esau's heart. That is why he sent the gifts ahead: he thought Esau might be coming to kill him.

Hebrews explains what was working in Esau: “Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled”. Looking diligently means looking within yourself. The root of bitterness is a hidden sin under the ground that nobody sees, but over time it springs up and troubles you. It distorts your thoughts and your perception, so that things you once saw clearly, with eyes anointed with eye salve, are no longer pure to you.

“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” Profane means devoted to what is not sacred, secular rather than religious: Esau was a carnal man, a man of the field, whose religion is sin. When we follow the carnal ways of Esau, we throw away our birthright, the kingdom of heaven. Hebrews says “for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.” Hold on to a bitter spirit and you are a spiritual Edomite, and you will find the same place of no repentance on that day.

An officer drew the parallel: “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” Christ came “that he might destroy the works of the devil”, so we cannot move in the devil's spirit and think we move in Christ's. Whoever does not love his brother is not of God. If there is an offense, deal with it by Matthew 18:15, not by sowing discord in the congregation. “For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” The spiritually minded man seeks to gain his brother, not keep him as a rival to get back at, “Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God”.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:19-20
precepts.why:
Esau cried, “Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing.” Is that true? Go back to Genesis 25. Esau came from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”. “And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.” There was no trickery. Jacob asked him straight, and it was up to Esau to say no. Esau said, “what profit shall this birthright do to me?” Jacob made him swear, because the word of that man is no good, just as with the four hundred and some treaties they broke. Scripture sums it up: “thus Esau despised his birthright.”

So Esau was lying and playing the victim. The Psalm describes it: “Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.” “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Did we not just read the slander? He tricked me two times. Nowhere does scripture show Jacob dealing with deceit over the birthright. They were liars from the beginning, because they moved in the same spirit as their father Cain, who was of the wicked one.

It is how they do today: throw the rock, hide the hand, and as soon as the other side hits back, run to the UN as the victim. Now all of a sudden he cares about the birthright, just as his children want to stand in our place claiming to be the Jews and the people of the book. Where was that energy when he threw it away for something to eat, or today for money and fame?

You got the children of God and you got the children of the devil; there is no in between. You either got the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The same Psalm says to the wicked, the white man, “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” “Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” They say in God we trust and swear on the Bible while doing nothing the scripture says.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept”, but that was worldly sorrow. “For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.” We must come to the Lord sincerely, because of those who wait, God says, “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:” “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. “Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way”. We all have to examine ourselves so we are not moving in that same spirit.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 3:16-17
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses”. That is purging the old leaven. We had to do it physically, but it is something spiritual today. So what is your house today? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” You, me, we are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God is to dwell in us because our temple was destroyed.

Look at how we purge leaven from the house. Brothers dump out the toaster, sweep underneath the floor mats and in the corners where stuff builds up. There is not one grain of yeast in the house. Meanwhile the brother has an evil eye toward another brother, or is bitter toward his wife, or vice versa. We sweep our houses with diligence; we must do the same with our spirit, because we are the temple of God.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” You will pull this out on a brother in the street: brother, you got tattoos, you got the devil on you, you are defiling your temple. We know tattoos are wrong. But meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If you are out there with the leaven of bitterness in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if he and you do not repent.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
Exodus 12:15 says, “whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” What is that really saying? How do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps into your mind and you say, damn, I don't like that brother. You are spiritually consuming it, entertaining sin and not purging the leaven from your house. That is how you get cut off from your people, and this is a serious thing.

How you get cut off: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Christ is our Passover, who set the example. That is the gift, the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins, because we are in a wicked place.

And Exodus 13:7 says “there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” We do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, Passover or not. Don't be the brother who does not throw the bread out but puts it in his storage closet and brings it back when Passover is over: laying the bitterness aside for the season and picking right back up hating the brother. That is not the spirit. Throw it out. Let it go.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20
precepts.why:
Some brothers say, I am going to tuck mine in, tuck away my hatred and my bitterness and save it for later. Paul answers that: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?”

We are not our own. So when we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, whatever sins we deal with, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He is our Passover, our sacrifice; he bought us back, twice he bought us back. So we do not own our bodies to even have the angle to defile our temple. When a brother lends you something, you are supposed to take extra care of it. Christ gave us our bodies and bought us back again, and we need to keep them like brand new.

“For ye are bought with a price”: with Christ's blood. Then, “therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” We have to use our bodies to glorify him in every way possible, and our spirit too, because both belong to God. When we hold back malice, hatred for our brothers or hatred for our wife, we put that on Christ, and it is not of the Lord. We have to let go of that spirit.

That is the leaven Exodus 12:15 says to put out of your house: not only the yeast on the box, but the bitterness tucked in when Bishop comes around and let out again when he leaves.

thread.label: Exodus 20:17
thread.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.

classes.title: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.label: 2 Peter 1:4-5
precepts.why:
To covet is not simply to desire. It is to want what belongs to another inordinately: you violate God's laws to get it. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”. The daughter belongs under the father just like everything else in his house. Go around him to get her, never telling the fathers or the elders, and you have coveted. To entice is to allure, to bait, to induce to evil; it is trickery and deception. “My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not”. And “Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: if you love the sister, how did you use ill means to get her?

Peter shows what we are supposed to be doing instead: “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. And beside this, giving all diligence”.

As brothers and sisters come in here, you are supposed to be escaping these worldly elements and truly repenting. When you look across the aisle, you are supposed to be looking for righteousness, not just her behind. Taking your sister for lust is the corruption that is in the world, and the same thing goes on on the other side. A man who talks to you under cover, without your father and without the leadership, does not have good intentions; the fact that he didn't do it the right way shows you where his mind is.

Do it with diligence, the right way. When we announce our marriages we say, this is the day the Lord has made between you two; you can bring forth righteousness right here, and the Lord, the angels and everybody are in agreement with it. When you do things the right way, you have a whole community behind you. The fathers and the elders have the vantage point: we see down the road where it is going, and we make the decision as fathers.

precepts.label: Leviticus 6:4-5
precepts.why:
Exodus 22:17: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins”. He has to pay, but he still is not getting the daughter. Somebody might say, he paid, so he gets to take her. Leviticus 6 shows the principle: “Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away”.

Took violently away. To entice that daughter against her father's wishes is to violate him, and violation is violence. That is the same reason a man who steals an ox must “restore five oxen for an ox”: the owner was violated, and restitution is paid for the violent act against him.

“or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten”. The recent matter was deceit. Her fathers didn't know anything about it, the leadership didn't know anything about it, nobody knew until her sister discovered it, and they still weren't going to say anything. How are you going to come up later saying, here's the law?

“Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering”. The principal is the actual thing taken, and the fifth part is added on top. So you are not getting the daughter, and you still have to pay the fathers. That is why the judgment goes forward: we will not leave that kind of example for the rest of the sisters, to be beguiled by a wicked brother who says we're applying Exodus 22:16. That's a damn lie.

precepts.label: Matthew 19:3-8
precepts.why:
The Pharisees came to Christ “tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?” They were trying to use Moses' law, the writing of divorcement in Deuteronomy 24. Christ took them back to the beginning: “Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?” From the beginning there was no such thing as divorce. What are you talking about, quoting Moses? It's the same as a negro trying to quote Exodus 22:16.

“Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder”. God did not put these backdoor marriages together. That's why love worketh no ill to his neighbour: you will not do evil and call yourself love. You don't love anything but your own lust.

“Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so”. The only reason Moses had to bring in that negro-proof law is that we were hard-headed and gave Moses hell. It is a failsafe law, a kind of bylaw to keep us from going all the way wicked. You are not supposed to be in failure at all for it even to come up, and quoting one after you went off and did wrong does not make you righteous.

That is covering violence with the garment: “for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the Lord of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously”. The Pharisees enlarged the borders of their garments, and the fringes represent the laws. A man who deceived to get a sister and then gives her a so-called law from the Bible is covering his violation with the law. Sisters and brothers, watch yourselves, hold yourselves in the diligence of the scriptures, and stop playing games.

precepts.label: John 10:30
precepts.why:
“Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord.” One mind, one body: we start with the order first. The Lord our God is one Lord, and Christ shows what that oneness looks like: “I and my Father are one.”

Is there a division between Christ and his Father? No. They are on one accord. Two persons, the Father and the Son, and yet one, because the Son is in full agreement with the Father.

That is what we as a body have to be: one, in unison, in sync. This is why we have been able to accomplish the amazing things we have in this body, in this congregation: because we are one. Many of our people today have a social religion, more like a superstition, believing what society told them to do. We rely on the scriptures and believe on the Lord as it is written, and the scripture says the Lord is one and Christ is one with him.

precepts.label: John 5:30
precepts.why:
How are Christ and the Father one? Christ does what his Father tells him to do. “I can of mine own self do nothing”: Christ said it himself. “as I hear, I judge”: as I'm told, that's what I do. “and my judgment is just”: the things he does are justified, “because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He didn't do what he wanted to do; he did what the Father told him to do. You see how that works? He says, I don't do what I want to, I do what the Father tells me to, and yet the scripture says he and his Father are one.

That is how we keep the first commandment, to “love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might”: by keeping his commandments, and being one with the Father and the Son as they are one.

The psalm ends its first cry with, “O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?” How does the enemy blaspheme? By making our signs their signs. White Jesus is blasphemy. White angels are blasphemy. All these whitewashed images are blasphemy; it is evil.

To blaspheme is to speak evil of his name, his reputation. White Jesus is blasphemy. He died for all people, the gospel is for all people, all nations can be saved: blasphemy. He isn't the son of God, he doesn't exist, I'm an atheist, evolution: blasphemy. His name is blasphemed every day all around the world.

That is why the enemy is not only the one who burned the sanctuary and the synagogues, as Babylon and Assyria did. The enemy is also the one who keeps reproaching God's name by painting over his people, so that “We see not our signs.” We don't see statues of David or Solomon or Christ as black men; we see their images, their depictions.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:48

The psalm says of the enemy, “they set up their ensigns for signs.” What are their ensigns for signs? Cesare Borgia; Mother Mary, white Mary; baby white Jesus; white prophets; the Last Supper; the Sistine Chapel. Posing themselves as God, as the prophets, as the angels, as the heavenly Father: whitewashing our ensigns and making our ensigns their signs.

Maccabees shows it was done before: they “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The book of the law is our Bible, and the heathen sought to paint the likeness of their own images into it.

They made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain did it, Portugal did it, Britain did it, the Dutch, the French: they all did it, and they still do it. It was blasphemy back then, and it is blasphemy now.

That is why Asaph cries, “We see not our signs.” The heathen painted themselves into the book of the law, and our people no longer see their own images in the scriptures that were written about them.

precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Why is that good and pleasant? It's the only way we grow, keeping the commandments together as a unit; without unity there is disorder, and nothing gets built. But the reason it is so important is that we can't be stopped when we are unified. Moses shows it: “How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight”?

Unity. That's how we are going to do it: through us together, unified in Christ. Hence the name Israel United in Christ. We can move mountains. It's that type of unity we have to come to and understand, because without it, brothers, we won't do nothing.

Look at some of the others, not doing anything. They don't aspire to do anything; they're fine just where they're at, cool just being in the house, and they will keep doing videos from their garages. But we have worldwide goals. The vision here has been set at a worldwide standard. If you don't have worldwide aspirations, you're not going to do worldwide things. If you think small, you'll stay small. Shoot for the stars.

The sixty-man camp of 2013 showed it: that small number organized and unified set a standard in the nation, and today one phone call could bring a thousand men. That is one chasing a thousand and two putting ten thousand to flight, when brethren dwell together in unity.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 25:1
precepts.why:
“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” Some think this is just talking about a bunch of Negroes coming together, a bunch of brothers together, and that's beautiful. No, it is much more than that. If you are spiritual, you understand this unity is not gang banging, not the Hoovers, not the Omegas, Kappas and Alphas, not Freemasonry, none of that worldly nonsense some of us came out of. It is being unified in Christ; hence the name Israel United in Christ.

Sirach shows what unity God is beautified by: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren in what? In righteousness. The love of neighbours is not that oogly googly feeling, that's my neighbor, we're good friends; it is unity in righteousness, someone that shows care for their nation and their people. A man and a wife that agree together, in righteousness: a sanctified holy marriage that has come together in the Lord is a beautiful thing before the Lord.

Anything other than that is not beautiful, and the Lord is not beautified by it. Remember how Paul wrote to the different schools: you are puffed up, there are all types of schisms among you. That is not unity. To be unified means to come together in holiness and righteousness, the way God meant it to be and the way Christ told us to be. And that unification of the nation of Israel is the highest known threat to this evil world; it scares them.

But whoso confesses shall have mercy, and John shows why: “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins”. The Lord is faithful and just when we confess our sins.

That goes all the way back to Leviticus. When you brought your sacrifice before the priest, that was a public confession. You had to walk through the midst of all Israel with your offering.

Now we have the white man, his walls and his technology. We have VPNs: yeah, don't nobody know I'm on OnlyFans, I got a VPN, I'm broadcasting from the Philippines. No, brother, the Lord sees right through it.

So in order to get over the root of bitterness we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. Covering it will never prosper; confessing it is how we get the mercy we all want.

precepts.label: James 5:16
precepts.why:
Confessing is not only to the Lord. James says: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 says, no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess your fault, and a brother might say, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit. Woo, man, I feel a lot better. All of this is common. We all have levels of bitterness; some have a higher degree than others, but everybody deals with a level of bitterness, a level of lust, a level of lack of faith.

That doesn't mean getting on the public announcement. It means you see a godly man and say, hey Cap, hey D, I have this going on, I need help with it. They are going to help you. They are not going to say, brother, you got the devil on you, get away from me. It is Satan telling us otherwise.

That is whoso confesseth and forsaketh: confessing to the Lord, confessing one to another, and being healed, instead of covering the sin and letting the root grow.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:24
precepts.why:
“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

precepts.label: Matthew 8:28-33
precepts.why:
Isaiah says of the king of Babylon, “Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth”. Babylon is the United States of America, and hell is the destiny of its prideful rulers. Hell is a condition, and it is also a real place of torment and suffering. People say, you have nothing, you just walk around in purple clothes talking about the Bible. We know something you don't know: your ass is going to hell. Hell is a real place, and you're going there. We would not trade places with them for all the tea in China, for all the gold in Fort Knox.

Some Israelite camps teach there is no place of torment, and every time we teach about hell they make counter videos. So look at what the devils said to Christ. In the country of the Gergesenes “there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way.” “And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?”

The demons recognized Christ, and they knew there is a time appointed for torment. Then “the devils besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine.” An evil spirit needs a vessel to inhabit. “And he said unto them, Go.” The whole herd “ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters.” The Lord has a place where evil spirits go to suffer torment.

There is a time appointed when everybody who is evil, Israelite or not, is going to pay. Do not let any camp make you think you will escape judgment; they have no scripture to paint that picture.

Why would God make such a place? Because there are people on this earth who do not care about death, prison or you; they will do the most depraved things and laugh about it on the way to the grave. There has to be an extreme punishment for people who disregard life. If there were no hell and no place of suffering, God would not be feared. So there is a hell, God has it prepared, and the wicked, including wicked Israelites, are going into it.

precepts.label: Romans 11:1-2, 25-26
precepts.why:
Some Israelite camps use “all Israel shall be saved” to argue that even the wicked will escape hell. To see what Paul meant, start from the beginning of the chapter: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

Why did Paul open that way? Because of the conflict between the northern and southern kingdoms. The Jews thought God was not dealing with the northern kingdom anymore, since God had told them, you are not my people, and Hosea said that where it was said unto them, you are not my people, there they would be called the children of the living God. Paul, of Benjamin, was of the southern kingdom, and he answers, “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.”

“For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.” The mystery is that God is dealing with both the northern and southern kingdoms, which is why the chapter talks about them being grafted back in. God blinded a portion, the Jews, to salvation in Jesus Christ so that the gospel could be preached to the northern kingdom living as Gentiles, so they could come in. If you say you're an Israelite and you still don't understand this chapter after all these years, you're an idiot, and God is not dealing with you.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. That means both kingdoms, all twelve tribes, can be saved. It is not a license saying a murderer, an adulterer or a thief will be saved at the end no matter what. You see how stupid they are? Leaders who use this verse to say you are not going to hell are wise in their own conceits. There is a hell, and if you go against God you are going into it, Israelite or not.

precepts.label: Genesis 27:39-40
precepts.why:
Isaiah describes the king of Babylon as “He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger”. That is how they got where they are: they took this land with bloodshed, massacred the indigenous people, dragged Negroes to America against their will for hundreds of years and used us for free labor, and they are still always looking for a reason to start a war.

Isaac told Esau where that comes from: “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;” “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.”

Esau was given the fatness of the earth, and he lives by the sword. That is why they do not want anybody else to have a weapon. A nuclear weapon is a sword, and they rule because they can kill and destroy anything that comes against them. It is why they go to war with Iran over nuclear capability they have been talking about for thirty years, even when their own officials ask why.

It is also why the Pope calling for peace gets called weak. For a people who live by the sword, peace looks like weakness. But the same chapter of Isaiah says the one who weakened the nations will be cut down to the ground, because the pride of his heart has deceived him.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:27
precepts.why:
The first sign of a bitter brother is that he is easily offended; he will “make a man an offender for a word”. The next sign is that he holds grudges, the thing Leviticus 19:18 forbids: “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people”. And he is always revisiting past wrongs.

Proverbs names him: “An ungodly man diggeth up evil”. That is the bitter brother digging up evil, the plumber brother, digging up old ish. As we say up in the States, he's digging it up like he's a plumber.

“and in his lips there is as a burning fire.” That is deceit, and he is always hating. That is the brother with the banana on his lips, the certified hater like Cain: I don't like that. That's you.

So the one who makes a man an offender for a word is the same one who keeps digging up the old things. He lacks forgiveness, as Sirach 28 showed, and he will not let the past rest. Brother, you are not in the right spirit.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 20:22
precepts.why:
Another sign of bitterness is quiet resentment: they sit back and stew in silence. Sirach shows that brother: “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness”. He is the bitter bashful brother, brother BB.

“and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself.” He'll say, man, brother, everything good. Then he is told, brother, I need you to go do this, this and this, and he says, yes sir. The whole time he is thinking, I ain't feel like doing ish for that MF. He says yes sir to your face, and he has no intention in his heart of doing it.

That is the same bitter spirit as the one that makes a man an offender for a word, only hidden. The loud one digs up evil; the bashful one smiles and resents in silence. Either way he destroys his own soul, and he overthrows himself.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:1-6
precepts.why:
We say give the Lord no rest, make the time short, bring it on: when is he coming to get us out? We are trying to speed the Lord up. But the Lord has his timetable and a reason for the pace he is moving at, and when it is time for him to move, you can't stop it. Esau won't be able to stop it. “Therefore shall evil come upon thee; thou shalt not know from whence it riseth: and mischief shall fall upon thee; thou shalt not be able to put it off.” When all the planets have lined up, it is time to send Christ and the destroying angels to bring his people home, and if you are not ready, he comes as a thief in the night.

Ezra shows the mind of the Most High, his vantage point: “Before the fair flowers were seen, or ever the moveable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of angels were gathered together, Or ever the heights of the air were lifted up, before the measures of the firmament were named, or ever the chimneys in Sion were hot” … “before they were sealed that have gathered faith for a treasure.”

“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” The Most High made all of that, so we can't question that kind of understanding. We are not on the level to question how the Lord did things. Nobody did this but him, and by him alone it shall be ended.

So he sends Christ when he is ready to send Christ. We don't know the day or the hour, but we know we are in the season, and the enemies of the Lord include some of our own people siding with the oppressors by agreeing to be in sin and destroying their own people. That is not the agencies; that is negroes being wicked as hell, and negro is a mind state across all twelve tribes that was never supposed to be you. Knowing these things are coming, we need to get our minds and our spirits right.

precepts.label: Isaiah 40:13-17
precepts.why:
God's vantage point is far beyond the vantage point we think we have. People try to tell the Lord what to do: you can't love Jacob, you can't hate Esau, you can't forgive this one. So the Lord clears the deck and lets everybody know where he stands, and everybody else needs to shut the hell up.

“Who hath directed the Spirit of the Lord, or being his counsellor hath taught him?” Nobody. These are questions for us who are trying to push him. The dumb Christian talks about the way the Lord should be; shut up. “With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?” Who taught God knowledge? Nobody. God is the knowledge; how are you going to teach him?

Having asked questions we can't answer, he proclaims what it is: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket.” You walk with a pail of water and one drop falls out; you won't even notice it. All the nations put together are that one drop. They “are counted as the small dust of the balance”: not big dust, small dust on the scales, weighing nothing. “He taketh up the isles as a very little thing”: the Polynesian and Hawaiian islands, very little, nothing.

“And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.” If they burnt up all the meat in Lebanon, it would not be sufficient for him to accept the Arabs, Ishmael, as his people. Only the Israelites are his people; that is why the first verse of the chapter says, comfort ye my people.

“All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.” Less than nothing is spit, a bowel movement. That is how the nations are counted to God, while to us he says comfort ye my people. That is the difference, and nobody can say anything against it. 2 Esdras 6:55-56 parallels it and calls them spittle: Ezra was quoting Isaiah. The supreme power has it set up the way he wants it set up.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:64
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” Jeremiah 23 really talks about the essence of hirelings. How do they scatter the sheep? In Christianity they scatter them into the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the holiness church, whatever denomination. We are being divided rather than united as the twelve tribes of Israel. Even in the time of Christ there were the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the Stoics, the Epicureans and the Herodians; we were being scattered then, and it's happening today.

Moses said where it would lead: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Under these wood gods, like Christianity with the old wooden cross, and the many denominations under Islam, our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, even in Judaism.

Remember, this is about Israelites; it is not so much talking about Esau. “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: driven them away from the truth that they are the Israelites of the twelve tribes. But the Lord says “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them”.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 3:15
precepts.why:
Against the hirelings who scatter the flock, the Lord promises “I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them: and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall they be lacking”. Jeremiah shows what they will feed us with: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

Knowledge and understanding of what? God's laws. It isn't talking about feeding them with jumping up and down, screaming and foaming at the mouth.

Right now we are lacking as a race, as a people. We are lacking knowledge, wisdom and understanding; and when you break it down, we are lacking rulership, dominion of the earth, our own country, a fortified family, a nation. We are lacking everything. Pastors after God's heart, feeding us the laws, are the shepherds who end that lack.

precepts.why:

Zechariah gives the call to come out: “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord”. The north country is North America; flee from North America.

“for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord”. We are not just in North America. That is why Jeremiah says “from all countries whither I had driven them”: the 12 tribes were scattered to every corner, and the gathering is from all of them.

“Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Who is that? Judah. That is the “Judah shall be saved” of Jeremiah 23, where in the days of the righteous Branch, Christ, Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely; remember we were split into two kingdoms.

“for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” Meaning we are his favorite. We are God's favorite. And the end of it is “they shall dwell in their own land”. That is what we are lacking: we don't have our own land. The Lord who brought Israel out of Egypt will be known as the Lord who brought his favorite people out of the north country and set them in their own land.

precepts.label: Acts 14:22
precepts.why:
“They say still unto them that despise me, The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace”. They are speaking to people who really hate God. At the sit down, the man with the hat kept saying that when tribulation comes, we're not going to be here; the church won't be here. Christians just lie and tell you there's going to be peace.

But Paul and Barnabas were “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The only way we're entering the kingdom of God is through much tribulation. So what Bible are these Christians reading?

That is why Jeremiah says “Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.” A vision of their own heart is their own mind, what they feel at that moment: I don't know who this is for, but God has a message for you. It is not coming from the Bible, and the Bible says tribulation.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:27-31
precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.”

In all the lands we were scattered, “if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul”, meaning do everything God says to do. “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice; (For the Lord thy God is a merciful God;) he will not forsake thee”.

When thou art in tribulation, even in the latter days: so these Christians don't know what they are talking about when they say the church won't be here. Israel is in tribulation in the latter days, and Jeremiah said “in the latter days ye shall consider it perfectly.” Our people will not repent unless they get a foot up their behind; death makes people reconsider their ways. We say we are Christians, we serve the same God, and the white man doesn't give a damn about that. But the Lord is merciful: seek him with all the heart and he will not forsake us nor forget the covenant of our fathers.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:13-18
precepts.why:
“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was during the time of Adam. Ezra says “the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. Strait things is tribulation.

So all Israel is going to go through tribulation, the righteous and the unrighteous. “they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The false prophets say “No evil shall come upon you”, but “a whirlwind of the Lord is gone forth in fury”, and it will not return until he has performed the thoughts of his heart.

What we see on the news, death after death, is just the beginning. A young black girl tied to a tree with a ratchet strap, the kind trucks use to hold down wood, and they call it suicide. Tonya Miller, 27, and Juliana Enza, 16, found hanging from trees, ruled suicides; look at all these names. They can insult our intelligence with this because we are not unified and not connected to the Lord; there is no consequence. They don't do it to the Chinese or Japanese. And it is not only the men: all you independent women, get ready. I don't see color; well, color sees you. It's going to escalate. They won't ask what God you serve: you're in the image of God, and they will come for all the melanated brothers and sisters. The righteous suffer the strait things and hope for the wide.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:24
precepts.why:
“For thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.” Who is that I? Christ. And Christ said who he came for: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

That is what Christ was doing, seeking out the lost sheep of Israel, and that is what Paul and the apostles were doing after him. That was the great commission in Matthew 28:19.

So when Ezekiel says “I will seek that which was lost”, that's our people. The lost sheep Christ was sent to are the same sheep God promised to search out and deliver “out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day”: all places, countries and lands.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:4-5
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says God will search his sheep and gather them from the countries. Who does the gathering? “He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.” He calls to the heavens from above: those are the angels he's calling to. And to the earth: the earth are the prophets, you and me on the earth.

“Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Those are the twelve tribes of Israel. So he's telling the prophets, gather the twelve tribes, and he's telling the angels, gather the twelve tribes.

That is the promise of Ezekiel 34: “I will bring them out from the people, and gather them from the countries, and will bring them to their own land, and feed them upon the mountains of Israel.” The good pasture is the kingdom.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:31
precepts.why:
“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” These are the angels of Psalms 50, called from the heavens to gather.

Did he say gather everybody, all people? No. They gather his elect, and his elect are Israel. It's the same gathering Ezekiel spoke of: “so will I seek out my sheep, and will deliver them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark day.” The four winds are all the places, countries and lands where our people were scattered.

The prophets gather on the earth, the angels gather from the heavens, and it is the elect, the sheep of the house of Israel, who are gathered.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
Who are the elect the angels gather in Matthew 24? Isaiah answers: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name.” Israel is God's elect.

So there's no contradiction between the New Testament and the Old Testament. Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the angels gather the elect, and the elect is Israel. Ezekiel's sheep, Matthew's elect and Isaiah's elect are the same people.

The contradiction comes from these false pastors, these hireling pastors, who tell the people it is everybody. The Lord said: “I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick.” That's our people: we were broken, we're the sick ones. “but I will destroy the fat and the strong”: he is going to destroy the nations. “I will feed them with judgment.”

precepts.label: Psalms 149:1-5
precepts.why:
“Praise ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints.” The saints are the twelve tribes God gathers.

“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him”: because we have not been rejoicing in our creator, we've been rejoicing in the white man. “let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: for so long we've been joyful in the white man.

“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.” He doesn't take pleasure in all races on the planet, only in his people.

“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds.” That's the rest right there. It is what Ezekiel promised the gathered sheep: “there shall they lie in a good fold, and in a fat pasture shall they feed upon the mountains of Israel. I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord God.”

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10-11
precepts.why:
When the voice told Peter, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common”, Peter would have had to go to the Old Testament to explain what God had cleansed. He would go to Ezekiel 37: “I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” And whom was he gathering, and from where? “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”: they were living among the Gentiles, the nations. He gathers them, cleanses them, and takes the two kingdoms, the stick of Judah and the stick of Joseph in the hand of Ephraim, and makes them one.

Hosea shows the same joining: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” That is the two sticks becoming one in the Lord's hand.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The northern kingdom, cast out among the heathen and called not my people, would be called the sons of the living God again. That was the prophecy, and that is why Peter could not call those men common: the time had come, Peter, we have to gather them together, bring them together.

And guess what: that is happening now. It has been going on since back then until now. We are out in South America gathering God's people, out in Africa gathering God's people, and here in the States bringing God's people back together, Judah and Israel under one head.

precepts.label: Baruch 4:1
precepts.why:
Hosea says of Israel that “they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Baruch shows what breaking out is: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Such as leave the law, or break away from it, shall die. That is what they break out means.

So the sins Hosea lists, swearing, lying, killing, stealing and committing adultery, are a breaking away from the book of the commandments. Where the law is left, there is no truth, no mercy and no knowledge of God in the land, because truth is the application of God's laws, and the laws of God are not being taught or enforced.

And once they break out, blood toucheth blood: violence, hatred, killing against each other. The law endures for ever and keeping it is life; leaving it is death. The truth is the only thing we have to get up out of here. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death.

That is why the land mourns. If those same sins abide in the body, adultery, stealing, lying, swearing, not applying God's laws, hatred, violence, the congregation will not grow and will not flourish. As leaders we must teach the laws, hold people accountable to them, and be the example ourselves, so people can see there has to be a change in the way we move and how we think.

precepts.label: Amos 3:3
precepts.why:
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” That is the answer to the one who decides not to congregate with the body on the Sabbath, or to congregate partially, and then congregates with somebody that has been put out of the body. That is out of order, and it is sin.

The Sabbath is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. We cannot cook, we cannot buy, we cannot sell on the Lord's Sabbath day, and we must congregate, because it is a holy convocation. There is no way around that; you cannot decide not to do it. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us.

People do otherwise because we rationalise in our minds what we think is acceptable and what God will be all right with. God said, No, my commandments are straight; this is what I told you to do. Our biggest problem is trying to put our own thoughts in on how it should be done, but the Lord said, Your thoughts are not my thoughts. It is not hard. It only gets hard when we start to rationalise.

Imagine if that is how we started, people coming and going, this one wearing a yarmulke, this one wearing that. That is not how you build God's army. There must be structure, and the leaders are the example, the representative of what a godly Israelite looks like. When there is no agreement in the body, there is no truth in the land, and the land mourns.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:23-24
precepts.why:
Hosea ends with a promise: “he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.” What is the analogy of the former and latter rain? It's going to be a blessing. When we harvested crops, we looked forward to the rain coming. We needed the rain to come. When it didn't rain, we knew the Lord wasn't dealing with us. That's how he punished us.

We read that in Deuteronomy 28: “And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.” That is what it looks like when the rain does not come: the heaven shut like brass, the ground hard as iron, and powder and dust in place of rain.

So when Hosea says the Lord will come unto us as the rain, it is the curse being lifted. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us”. We were torn by captivity and slavery, and he will heal us, meaning redeem us out of this situation. After two days, two thousand years, he revives us, and in the third day he raises us up to who we are, to our identity.

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”: if we follow on to apply what God tells us to do, then shall we be bound up and healed. The rain the Lord withheld in the curses comes back as a blessing, and that blessing will be in the application of his laws.

precepts.label: Isaiah 46:8-11
precepts.why:
Habakkuk stood on his tower demanding answers: how long are we going to be in this captivity? The Lord answered, “the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come”. Now that we know what time we are in, Isaiah says, “Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors.”

Be men and use your mind. God gave the sons of God a mind to envision greatness, to see things in the mind before the hands build them. He gave you that vantage point so you can set up a congregation and make sure evil does not come among the brothers and sisters. O ye transgressors: change.

“I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”. God declared the end before he said, Let there be light. Everything falls in the path he wants it to fall. He knew from ancient times that the fourth bird from the mother hen would fly over Wyoming on March 7th, 2028. You say that bird is insignificant; he says, I need that bird to do that because it is connected to something else you don't know about. That is his vantage point.

“Calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man that executeth my counsel from a far country”. While he causes that bird to come from the east, he calls another man to execute his judgment. “I have purposed it, I will also do it.” A sparrow shall not fall to the ground unless the Most High causes it. Everything is under his auspices; he knows why he holds the armies back so the earth is not destroyed. You and I are not on that level, and we try to move God while we will not keep the commandments. The only thing we need to do is obey what he said.

That is why the vision will not lie. We cannot reason out why he calls that insignificant raven, but in God's overall plan it is necessary, and the end he declared from the beginning will surely come.

precepts.label: Isaiah 55:7-11
precepts.why:
Habakkuk was told, “the just shall live by his faith”, by the words of the book of our fathers. Isaiah shows what that faith requires of us: “Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.”

Those of us in wickedness must forsake it, and forsake the unrighteous thoughts of lasciviousness, lust, adultery and fornication. Get that thing out of your mind. He will pardon us if we are sincere, not pretending while on the back end doing evil and thinking nobody sees. The Lord understands the heartbeat of a raven, how many times a bird's heart will beat its whole life, and you think he don't see your black ass? You are playing with death.

“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways”. Looking down from heaven on the whole planet, he sees everything we cannot. Our only vantage point is our immediate circumference, and we cannot take that and tell the Lord what to do.

It works the same in the congregation. A manager of a department sees his space; the leadership over all the departments sees the interactions between them, and why something is happening here and not there. Leaders are in front to protect the flock because they see the danger you do not see. The man on the tower sees it coming and sounds the trumpet with a certain sound, so the people know what to prepare for.

“So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please”. As the rain waters the earth and does not return void, everything the Lord sends has a purpose. So when leadership says, brother, leave the sister alone, or sister, leave the brother alone, there is a vantage point you do not see, and if you will not hear it, it gets revealed in judgment after you done laid with the dude. Follow the steps, betrothal and the whole nine, and the council can bless the wedding and counsel the trouble in the flesh. Say to hell with all of it, and you are saying you have nothing to do with us.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:2
precepts.why:
Habakkuk said, “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. The watchman on the tower sees what the people below cannot. Peter gives the elders that charge: “Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight thereof”.

Listen to the wording: taking the oversight. The leaders stand at a vantage point the flock cannot see. From the experience and the level they have reached over their years in the truth, they see what younger men and younger women do not, and God gave them revelation through the scriptures to see how to guide you. If we believe there is a God, and that Christ is the brain of this whole operation, then we are supposed to trust the men he set up.

But a lot of brothers and sisters in the congregation get horny and antsy and will not follow the counsel. Then they end up asking the same leadership whose oversight they did not trust to counsel them on the matter after the fact. That is completely backwards, and nobody does that but us. That is the negro mind.

“Not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind”. That is for the leadership: they feed the flock willingly and take the oversight because they love their people. Nobody is getting paid to do this. They do it of a ready mind, watching from the tower until the vision the Lord appointed comes.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:32-33
precepts.why:
“Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh”. Christ is saying, pay attention to the seasons. Watch the fig tree; when the branches are tender and the leaves come out, you know summer is near by how the trees are changing.

“So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” We do not know the day and we do not know the hour, but we know we are in the season. The prophets wrote down what was coming, and now we actually see it: the missiles sitting in the silos ready to rock, the mushroom cloud Isaiah 34 speaks of. They did not have that when Malachi brought this out, but it is here now, letting us know what time we are in. You are not going to get a bigger sign than that.

So that is where we are: the destruction is even at the doors, and here we are playing games. That is what Malachi was saying: “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.” Smite the earth with destruction. So we had better remember the law of Moses, the laws and the commandments, and keep them, so that we are not caught off guard when that day comes. Knowing these things are coming, our minds and our spirits need to be right.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:7-10
precepts.why:
Ezra is still dealing with the mind of God. The Lord had said all things “were made through me alone, and through none other: by me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” That is the smiting of the earth with a curse. We cannot move God's timetable; not a sparrow falls without the Father, and he has millions of things lined up that we are not even aware of. You are trying to move God with your hastiness, and yet you will not even keep the commandments.

Then Ezra asks for the sign: “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” When shall this wicked rule end? It is the same question the disciples asked in Matthew 24: when shall these things be?

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.” That is the only clue given, and the people in the churches do not even know who Esau is, so they are completely lost. Bishop Nathanyel's class on the Achilles heel goes with this like cookies and milk.

“For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Once we find out who Esau is, see how he is acting on this earth and read about him in the Bible, we know the time is near, even at the doors. And Jacob is the beginning of what follows: Jacob is going to rule; that is the kingdom. Seeing all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought we to be? Our minds need to be on that level.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”. The other nations are in between, insignificant, affected by one or the other, and they will never rule.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:9-10
precepts.why:
The same transition of time is written in Revelation. “And the great dragon was cast out”: that is Esau, the red dragon, the Romans. That was the Roman Empire that came into our heaven, meaning our kingdom, destroyed Jerusalem and cast us into captivity. The heaven Esau is going to fall from is his ruling kingdom right now. It is not a fight at creation where Satan got kicked out of heaven; that is a perversion of Isaiah 14.

Satan does what the Most High tells him. In Job the Lord asked Satan where he came from, and Satan could not touch Job because of the hedge around him, which is the hedge we want around us. In Kings, when Ahab was to be persuaded to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead, an evil spirit said he would be a lying spirit in the mouth of his prophets, and the Lord sent him. The Lord has control of everything. Here in Revelation 12 is when Christ destroys these demonic forces.

“That old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”: going all the way back to Cain, back to Eve. Devil means evil; Satan means adversary. That is the white man; he fits it to a tee. And he has never been white: not nasty white, not beige, not off-white. He is red. Stop lying when you look at him.

“Which deceiveth the whole world”: he made everybody on the planet believe Christ looks like Charles Manson, when the Bible gives a full description of Christ as a black man with woolly hair and feet like brass burned in a furnace. That is great deception.

“He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: his missionaries, his black preachers and ministers, imps of Satan to destroy our people. Christianity is the perfection of slavery. In chains, being whipped, we still wanted freedom; but Christianity is the greatest dope of all, and it put us so far to sleep we do not even want to be free. It destroyed us from within.

When the Lord casts this devil down and smashes all that Christian garbage and all those lies, then: “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down”. When these devils go down, we rule. That is Jacob, the beginning of the world that follows.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:15-16
precepts.why:
“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.” Christ is the firstborn of every single creature, the first created. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

By Christ were all things created in heaven and in earth. What is in heaven? All the angels, the host of heaven. Would Satan be a part of that? So who created those evil angels too? Christ did. So in the wilderness the creation is trying to tempt the creator. Think about that.

Satan knew that was the creator. But look at the time he came: “when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.” He came after the forty days of fasting, in a weakened state while in the flesh, and said, oh, I can surely tempt him; this is what he created me to do. Christ answered him with the word: “It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.”

The same thing applies among brothers and sisters. There is a time when you are in a weak state, spiritually, or physically from surgery or pain, and Satan comes: nobody called to check on you, but here I am; they don't know you like I know you. You argue with your spouse and go for a drive, and guess who is in the passenger seat. He whispers memories you haven't thought of in years, like Cleopus Jenkins back in 73 with that Studebaker and the eight-track tape, and you think it is your own thought. He knows everything about you, from before you met your husband, because you were his employee.

If Satan tried to tempt his own creator, how much more is he going to tempt us? That is why we stay in the spirit and answer him the way Christ did.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:1
precepts.why:
Matthew writes “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”, and Isaiah had already written it: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

Matthew says “Galilee of the Gentiles”; Isaiah says “Galilee of the nations.” So the nations also means the Gentiles. Same land, same people, same word.

What we read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament. When the apostles and prophets spoke, they had to substantiate their points from what we call the Old Testament today. Whatever they said, they had to be able to justify it with that text. Matthew is not saying something new; he is showing the prophecy fulfilled.

This is the foundation for Acts 10. By the biblical text the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles, like strangers, like heathens. The New Testament shows Paul going out to find them scattered among the nations and bring them back to God, because the prophecy sent from the Old Testament was that the job was to raise up the 12 tribes of Israel again. The Gentiles of Galilee are Israelites that were scattered and cut off, and God is gathering them back.

thread.text: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:14
precepts.why:
“Ye are the light of the world.” Not the light of Brooklyn, not the light of one city: of the world. When the Lord sent us out, he sent us out as a light to the whole world, and Matthew 24 shows how far that light has to go.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” How is it going to be preached in all of the world if you have no plans, no plan of action, no implementation to do anything worldwide? How are you the guys if you ain't got global goals and you ain't touching the ends of the earth?

The Lord sent his prophets with vision, with goals, with aspirations to take it to the ends of the earth. That is why leadership puts things in place: “Where there is no vision, the people perish.” This is a global mission, and our aspirations and goals have to be set to a global standard, not a local one.

So the light of the world is a people carrying the gospel of the kingdom to all nations, and the end does not come until that witness has gone out.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:11
precepts.why:
“The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Our people are the remnant, scattered to the four corners of the world.

How are these people going to be able to rise out of these places if they were never told? That is why this gospel has to have a global standard, preached to the whole world. If your leadership ain't talking about covering the earth, they're not the guys. Don't waste your time.

They ridicule us now: y'all going over there to Africa, y'all in India, you went to Australia, you went to Papua New Guinea. We don't give a damn how anybody feels about it. Negro, you do lack the understanding of this Bible; you do err, not knowing the scriptures. The people have been scattered to the four corners. How are you going to reach them if your aspirations are just down the street, if you want to be known for Times Square or a street corner?

Where would we be today if this truth had stayed in Harlem, if it never left the streets of Brooklyn? Where a lot of these other camps are. Being the light of the world means going where the remnant was scattered, to the islands of the sea, and telling them who they are.

Luke gives the same word Christ spoke in Matthew 12: “And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.” It shall not be forgiven.
