precepts.label: 1 Peter 4:10
precepts.why:
“But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.” Everyone has a gift, but it goes toward the same goal in unison. It is not just for you. However the manifestation comes, there are different gifts given so that you can profit with all the nation.

Peter: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.” Where does the gift come from? The Lord. And what is it used for? To minister one to another.

You have not been given a gift just for you. If you have been given a gift and you only use it for yourself, it did not come from the Lord; it is not of the Lord. You are supposed to use that gift to benefit your nation and your people. That is why you were given it. If your gift only glorifies you, it is not about Christ; it is about you.

“as good stewards”: now you understand the stewardship program. These gifts are to be used for the building of the body, so that we can do what we need to do as a nation. The word of wisdom, the word of knowledge, faith, all given “to every man to profit withal.”

precepts.label: Philippians 2:4
precepts.why:
When you have these gifts, what do you do with them? Paul: “Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” How can I apply this gift to help somebody? How can I use what I know to help somebody else, to benefit my people, to benefit the school? What little brick can I put in that is going to bring us to where we need to be? That is the mind frame we must have when we function as a body.

Take the gift of reaching people. Some brothers can get a flyer into anybody's hand, even people who do not want one. The man walks off from one brother and tells him to go screw himself, and then another brother walks up the same way and the man leaves with a flyer in his hand saying, all right brothers, y'all take care. People have different gifts.

You might have used that gift in the world to hustle and get over on people, but that is not why you were given it. When you come into this truth and your mind is renewed, you understand: God gave me that gift so I can get the word out, relate to people, and show them thus saith the Lord.

If you are not using that gift for the Lord, the Lord did not give it to you; Satan gave it to you. God gives these gifts with purpose, “to profit withal”: every man looking on the things of others.

precepts.label: Romans 12:6-8
precepts.why:
“Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”. These are the different gifts, administrations and operations. Whatever gift you have been given, if it is prophecy, prophesy with everything you have; whatever the Lord gave you, that is what you give.

“Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching”. Everybody stays in their lane. You work within the gift and skill set you have been given, and you do not try to force things that are not you. Size is not everything, but at camp you cannot put the brother who is 105 pounds at the front sentry. He might be the fire teacher, or real good on flyers, but if the wind blows it will carry him away and we will not have a front sentry.

When you are outside of your character, things get messy. If you pretend to be something you are not, you may be put in that position, and the person who should be there cannot operate the way the body needs, and we lack in different areas. Years ago a certain brother was put over the bills; one Sabbath the lights were off at the school. We learned that day he is not the one to put over the bills. We found where he belongs, and he is operating within his place now. Everybody does not belong everywhere.

“Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.” Everyone in their office, in their proper position. That is what Paul means when he says the one Spirit is “dividing to every man severally as he will.”

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 12:12
thread.text: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.

classes.title: Member's In The Body

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:4-6
precepts.why:
“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” A body has many parts that all work together: the heart that pumps blood, the brain that thinks, the arms and legs that move. We at Israel United in Christ are not many bodies. IUIC Austin, OKC, Atlanta and Arkansas are many members, but not different bodies. We are one body, in the same mind and the same spirit, so wherever you travel it should have the same feel and the same teachings.

Ephesians says it: “There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

There are not multiple ways, no matter what Oprah said. There are not different types or different forms of God and how to worship God. There is only one way, one truth, and to be in alignment with it you must do exactly what the body is supposed to do: keep the commandments and have faith in his Son.

That is what brought us together. If fellowship, friendships and relationships are what brought you here, you are in the wrong place. We are brothers and sisters who decided to do what God said against all odds and all the influences of the world; we don't care if you look at us funny.

We keep coming back to that soundness, that unity, that oneness in Christ. Anybody teaching anything other than that does not belong here. There is no separatism in the nation and no separatism in the body of Christ. We are all one.

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 12:12-20
thread.text: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.

classes.title: Member's In The Body

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:11-13
precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” The Lord is not the author of confusion; he is of order. When he brings in these different talents, gifts and members, he brings them for a purpose that serves one thing, with different functions. Paul shows it: “And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”.

All of it was for one goal: “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. Though they had different offices and administrations, it was all for the perfecting of the saints.

You see it in the teachers today. Not all of them focus on the same things: some focus on prophecy, some on organization and structure, some on marriage, and you can see, that's his specialty. Learning from the deacons as the first internet member, you could see, he's good at this, I need some of that, and you learn where to go and what to glean.

What office can we say we don't need? If you think like that, you're not nation building; you haven't been given the vision. Back in the day some camps said, don't do anything with the videos, just play them. But the video needs music, an intro, something alluring, so someone outside the scriptures says, let me look at this, and once the scriptures start hitting: oh snap, I know who I am now. That effort is a member doing its part.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 4:10
precepts.why:
Every member was set in the body for a reason, so Peter says: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.”

Shame on you if you come in here and sit on your hands, sit on the talent God has given you, and put forth no effort. If you have a craft or something to offer and you don't come in trying to show it and help, shame on you. You have been given that for a reason.

Your job is to utilize that gift and benefit your nation. Nobody should be bogging down your talents or making you stagnant; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching them to others where possible. That is being a good steward: the gift is ministered one to another, so the whole body is built up.

precepts.label: Proverbs 18:16
precepts.why:
“A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.” When you have a talent, when you're able to do something for the nation, at least come in and say, hey, I'm able to do this. We may say, all right brother, we'll utilize that gift a little later, or, we need you right here right now.

When the building in OKC was first acquired around 2017, it was trash. Out of nowhere brothers started coming out of the woodwork: I heard y'all teaching, I want to join. One saw them working on the building and said, I'm a carpenter, I build. It was dangerous in there, with downed wires, mold, asbestos and fiberglass floating; some brothers probably have lung damage to this day. He looked around and said, that's a fire hazard, you're going to die if you mess with that wire.

They were in there on the strength of the Lord, tearing down to build. The Lord brought those people in so they could build up the school. And right after completion that same brother disappeared: he served his purpose.

So a gift is not for hiding. It makes room for the man and brings him where the Lord wants him, and the body is built because every member brings what God gave him.

precepts.label: Matthew 25:24-28
precepts.why:
We have to utilize the gifts God gives us in this truth. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security. Realize that when you don't use it, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take the truth even further. The parable of the talents shows it; the talent is money, standing for the understanding God bestows on you.

“Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth”. He hid that understanding, that gift, and did nothing with it.

Watch what Christ says: “Thou wicked and slothful servant”. “Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.” Even if you couldn't do anything else, you could have put it with the exchangers so something could be reaped. “Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.”

We have seen it time and again: brothers and sisters with talents who hide them, or hold them over us: you can't do this without me. Know that yes, it can be done without you. If you can't be used, you are useless. But none of you are useless. We all have been called for a reason; there is something in you that you have to give to build the nation. The quicker we understand that, the quicker we get out of here.

precepts.label: Romans 12:3
precepts.why:
God has given us different gifts and different offices but the same mission. So Paul says, “to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” We are all expendable; we can all be replaced if we don't put something into this truth.

What happens when someone thinks more highly than he ought? Just because you're the knuckle, the one who keeps us safe, you think you're better than everybody else. When members begin to think they are more important than another, dysfunction comes into the body, and members start treating other offices as less important.

Where would we be without security? Unsafe. Without the brothers and sisters who clean the toilets, the kitchen and the floors? Infested with roaches and mice. Without the kitchen? Hungry as hell; some single brothers look forward to the Sabbath because they get a real meal and not the peanut butter and jelly they're used to. The Lord brought all these administrations together so we can function. Not one is more important; they all play a part.

Even leadership. A deacon is not better than you; he could die tomorrow and be the devil. He has to keep the commandments and believe on Christ just like you. At the gas company nobody says, oh, that's Deacon; they say, nigga, I had to come shut your stuff off for you to come see me. No one cares. If you start to think you're better because of your office, this body will suffer. Respect the sisters changing diapers; respect the brother folding flyers, who in his tenure has probably put a million flyers into the earth, and it may have been you who got one.

precepts.label: Philippians 2:3
precepts.why:
One body, many members, so “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.”

That striving spirit will unravel things, and people can see it when you move like that. Some of you security brothers, be careful. Because you're able to say move over here, move over there, you get ahead of yourself playing musical chairs: get up, go over here, no, sit right here, don't say nothing, hop on one leg, Simon says shut up. That's your brother; that's your sister. Deal with somebody the way you want to be dealt with.

Yes, some folks are hard-headed and act a straight fool, and sometimes you have to speak a certain way to let them know you're serious, because some don't understand organization. But no member is better than the next. We are all the same, working toward the same goal: we want the kingdom.

If we have this mind frame, esteeming each other better than ourselves, we are going to move mountains. That is what it means that the many members are yet but one body.

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 12:12-13
thread.text: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.

classes.title: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:10
precepts.why:
“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” Precepts were called for from the brothers, and the first was Paul's own plea to the same Corinthians: “Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you”.

That fits the body. The members are many, but they speak the same thing, and there are no divisions among them. Diversity does not mean division: a different administration, dealing with something you don't deal with, is not separate from you. And different roles do not mean inequality; no function or operation in the body is unneeded.

That is why, wherever you travel among us, it should carry the same teachings: we are one body, in one mind, speaking the same thing. It all goes back to endeavouring to keep the unity, until we all come “unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”.

precepts.label: Colossians 2:19
precepts.why:
The body is one and has many members, “so also is Christ.” Another brother brought Colossians: “And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.” It takes some explaining, but it speaks to the same thing.

The body is held together from the Head, Christ. From him the whole body, joined and banded together, has nourishment ministered to it and is knit together, and so it increases with the increase of God. The members do not hold themselves together; they are knit together by holding the Head.

That is the unity of the body: every joint and band ministering what it has been given, all fastened to the Head. Not holding the Head is how a body falls apart, and holding him is how it grows. That is why the next scriptures read go straight to Christ as the head of the body, the church.

precepts.label: Ephesians 1:22-23
precepts.why:
“so also is Christ”. How is the body Christ? Ephesians: “And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

God put all things under Christ's feet and gave him to be the head over all things to the church. Who is the head? Christ. Who is the body? The church. And who is the church? Us.

So when Paul says the many members are one body, “so also is Christ”, he means that we, the members, are his body, and he is the head over all of it. That is why there can be no division in the body: every member belongs to the same head, and the body is “the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

precepts.label: Colossians 1:17-18
precepts.why:
Christ is the head of the body. Colossians: “And he is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.”

Christ is before all things, and by him all things consist; everything holds together in him. He is the head of the body, the church, which is us. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead.

“that in all things he might have the preeminence”. The many members, with their different gifts, administrations and operations, are one body because they all come under one head, and he has the first place in everything. Make sure those precepts are written down: the body of 1 Corinthians 12 is the church, and Christ is its head.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 20:30-31
precepts.why:
The body has many members, and the different administrations in it are all to endeavour to keep the unity. So when we have these different administrations, we should not hide or neglect them. Sirach: “Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?”

That goes into wisdom, but also into the gift, because the wisdom God gives you comes through those gifts and through the spirit God puts on you. What profit is there in hiding wisdom or hoarding treasure? None. There is no profit in hiding the gift or the administration God has set you in and given you.

“Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.” A man who hides his folly is better than one who hides his wisdom, who hoards up the understanding God has given him. If you know you are good at something and God has blessed you with that spirit, use it to keep pushing the truth and growing the unity God has called us to, because we are all one body and it all goes to the same Spirit.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:11
precepts.why:
“For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body”. How many of us were dunked in water, the Baptist way? A church baptism in a green, filthy pond was shown, the brothers joking that it was pickle juice, but this verse is not talking about that. Baptized means cleanse. Write that down and look it up yourself: baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water, which is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

John says: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance”. If baptism always meant water, why would he need to say, I baptize you with water? It means, I cleanse you with water unto repentance. That was John's administration, water baptism, a tool to show forth repentance. It was never a requirement for the kingdom of heaven.

“but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear”. Somebody far mightier is coming, whose shoes John is not even worthy to hold. “he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. Did you hear anything about water? No. The baptism we must come under is through Christ: by one Spirit we are all cleansed into one body.

precepts.label: Luke 3:16-17
precepts.why:
Luke says the same thing, just in case anybody relapsed and wants to jump in the pickle juice: “I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire”. This is not talking about water.

“Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.” That is talking about judgment.

So you want the baptism of the Spirit, because the fire is coming to clean up everything else, and that is what Christ is coming with. The one Spirit that baptizes us into one body is the cleansing that gathers the wheat into his garner; the chaff that refuses it will be burned with fire unquenchable.

precepts.label: Romans 12:4
precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” God organizes the body, and God is who made us great. We are at the forefront, considered the vanguard, because God appointed us to be; if we move any differently than that, God will remove us and put somebody else there. Each of us was gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation.

Romans says the same: “For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”. Why do the members not have the same office? The heart and the brain function in different ways, but they come together to make the body function as one. The mind does not have the same function as the hand, and the hand does not have the same function as the foot. Every member functions, but they all need each other.

The body could not function with all hands or all elbows. If everybody comes in trying to be the hands, or everybody trying to be the feet, what will happen? Disorder. Everybody cannot be the head; everybody cannot be the shoulders. Everybody has their function.

So for those who think you are insignificant, just a regular Joe: God called you in here, and you have a mission and a purpose. You had better apply your gifts and your talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God. And preparing as a nation means more than food and water: we need lawyers, doctors, nurses, farmers. Go to school; master any skill, any trade, and bring that mastery back to benefit your nation.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 14:40
precepts.why:
God set the members in the body “as it hath pleased him”, and Paul says: “Let all things be done decently and in order.” The Lord is about order. He is not going to keep bringing the same member into the body, just hands and more hands; that is not how this works.

Understand how the scriptures use the body: it goes into functions. Can everybody be a teacher? Then who is going to read? Can everybody be the one for camp? Change is coming, because we have grown into a nation, and there are many talents and gifts, especially among the sisters, that have not even been tapped into yet.

We have looked at this from a war perspective, and it is all-out war outside; we need brothers prepared to spread this gospel. But in the functioning of this body, the Lord is showing that there are many more things we have to prepare ourselves for. If we don't, we will stay stagnant like others have. The camps that taught their people not to go to school, because Christ is coming soon, cannot open one building to this day, because they taught their people not to achieve greatness.

God brings the different members in for a purpose that all serves the same thing, with different functions. Back in 2016 the vision was set forth: Original Royalty, the kitchen, the school with the kids, security, video, music, all components of a society, the body of Israel under Christ working together for the common good of the whole nation. What was vision then is old news now; that is what order and vision do for a nation.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:24-26
precepts.why:
Paul says “For now we see through a glass, darkly”. What is the glass? Wisdom of Solomon answers it. “For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Keep in mind the whole time that we are talking about the glass.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom is the breath and the power of God. “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God”. That is the glass. Wisdom is the unspotted mirror of the power of God.

“and the image of his goodness”: this Bible is the image of his goodness, his greatness. The mirror itself is unspotted, but we see into it darkly. We do not have all of it fully. We know in part and we prophesy in part, even Paul, to whom God showed incredible revelations he did not show many of the other apostles.

That is meant to humble us. We have what is needful for salvation, but there are parts of this book we do not fully understand, so you do not know as much as you think you know. When that which is perfect is come, Christ, that which is in part shall be done away, and then we shall see face to face.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:18
precepts.why:
The glass is the mirror, the unspotted image of the power of God. So why do we see it “darkly”? Ephesians answers: “Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them”.

That is what it means when it says we see through a glass darkly. We do not have the full understanding of all these scriptures. The understanding is darkened, and there is ignorance in us still.

Then go back to Corinthians: “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” When we are with Christ, he is going to make this clear to us. Until then no one should vaunt himself as if he knows it all.

So “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.” Charity is the greatest because it is what keeps the body growing. People come in because they see how you move, how you conduct yourself and how you speak. You can teach all these scriptures with a photographic memory, but if you lack charity, if you are not kind and do not suffer long, the people will not stay.

precepts.why:
“evil communications corrupt good manners.” Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes things rise, and that is what bitterness does. The root of bitterness corrupts your spirit and messes with your attitude, and that angry influence spreads to others through words and through attitude.

So Proverbs warns: “Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go”. You see that brother is bitter; he is like that dangerous overgrown brush. There could be a viper in there, anything on the other side of that bush. Move.

“Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.” Now that bitter brother has put the bitter spirit on you. You got bit, like Bird Box, and now you are looking dumb. That is the snare right there.

That is why the scripture says be not deceived. Keeping company with the bitter brother is how the leaven gets into you. His evil communications will corrupt your good manners, and his offenses will reach others, starting with the first offense, the one in your own house.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 9:2
precepts.why:
“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord”. God is telling us to separate from these nations, these unbelievers. “and touch not the unclean thing”: do not follow their customs, their religions, their holidays or their politics. Only then will God receive us: “and I will receive you”.

What Paul instructed in Corinthians is nothing new. This is where it came from: “And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.” God instructed the twelve tribes to separate from the other nations and stop following the customs and traditions of those nations, and when they returned to him they separated themselves and confessed their sins.

Your churches have just never taught you that. They want to integrate; all churches want to integrate. Remember Philip Anthony: this is not a black church. Was that so moving? No, you sound like the devil now. He did not have to dance with the devil.

So coming out and being separate is the old path of Israel. The seed of Israel separates from the strangers, confesses its sins and the iniquities of the fathers, and then the Lord will be a Father unto us, and we shall be his sons and daughters.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:28-31
precepts.why:
Paul says “the sorrow of the world worketh death.” Here is what that worldly sorrow looks like: “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me”. When the Lord increases the affliction, after you have been wicked the whole time, now you are calling on the Lord: it's getting real down here, the persecution is on, I ain't got no food. You call, and the line says the number you have dialed is no longer available to you, dummy. You'll seek him early, like getting on a pre-call, and you still won't find him. You won't have any connection to the Lord on that day.

Why? “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. They had the carnal mind, the mind of Cain and Esau, and cast the word behind their back like their father did. “They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.” They literally threw the word behind their back, and a lot of our brothers and sisters do that. We all have to examine ourselves.

“Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.” If you are out there sowing sin, that is what you are going to reap.

That is Esau's sorrow. He sold his birthright, then realized, damn, I want that blessing back, and cried bitterly over what he himself threw away. So we have to be sincere when we come to the Lord and have the real godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation, to our inheritance, not to be repented of. We can't be out here faking the funk.

precepts.label: Proverbs 14:10
precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves”: not your neighbor, yourself. And you can do it, because “The heart knoweth his own bitterness”. Your mind knows its own bitterness. Brother, sister, you can't play confused when somebody asks, man, where is that bitterness coming from?

“and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.” So you can't say, oh Bishop, tell me what's going on with me. You know exactly what is going on in your mind. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is. We can say, brother, you're off, you ain't moving right, there is sin in there; we may not know it specifically, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.

This is a heavy topic. A lot of brothers and sisters are bitter. It came up in our congregation with a brother dealing with his wife, and then we came down here and saw the same thing, and it destroyed a household. If that spirit is left unchecked it can destroy the congregation. That is why each of us has to prove our own self: the heart already knows where the bitterness is.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
To examine ourselves we ask the Lord to do it with us: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me”. We ask the Lord to reveal the iniquity in us and not leave us blind to our own folly.

How is he going to do that? When you say, Lord, search me, that means you have to search the scriptures. The Lord ain't going to come down and say, open that door right there, let me see what's behind it. No, brother. You have to search the scriptures.

Then, in order to get over the root of bitterness, we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. We look to the scriptures and say, Lord, thank you for revealing that evil in me and showing me I have a bitter spirit, bitter toward my wife, toward the leadership, toward my brother, and we pray to the Lord to remove that spirit from us. That is how we prove our own selves, whether we be in the faith.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:22
precepts.why:
James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.” The heathen are the northern kingdom. Peter already knew this. God had shown him that he could not call any man common or unclean. He sat with them, and he convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, that God had granted them repentance unto life too.

“But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.” When certain came from James, Peter “withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.” Dissimulation means deception, hypocrisy, pretence, deceit, fakery: in other words, being fake. Paul said to him before them all, you are being fake like they were fake. Peter knew better, and he was corrected in front of everybody. He would have been embarrassed and ashamed.

But he repented. And as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake. So Peter wrote “Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently”.

Peter came back and taught it after he learned it: I was wrong. We cannot have fake love for the brethren, because God already showed me, and when I was put to the test I was influenced not to accept them. So the message now is, do not have feigned love for the brethren.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:11-13
precepts.why:
Isaiah shows what the “middle wall of partition” of Ephesians 2:14 looks like: the hatred, the enmity, the envy and the vexation between the two kingdoms.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” Has this happened yet? No. We are waiting on this second coming, waiting to be delivered again. That is why unification is so important: we have to go back to all these places, because our people are there. The Bible says they are in Assyria, in Egypt, in Pathros, in Cush, in Elam, and in the islands of the sea. We have a lot of work to do.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The outcasts are those who were kept afar off, living amongst the other nations as heathens, like Hellenized Jews. “The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.” The envy of Ephraim, the northern kingdom, is the wall of partition, and it is going to be gone. No more division: light skinned against dark skinned, look at your hair, look at my hair; the northern kingdom looking at us and us looking at them. Yes, Esau touched the northern kingdom; the southern kingdom has been through changes too. We look different today, but we are all the same people.

That wall is what Christ tore down. “He is our peace, who hath made both one”: the two sticks, Judah and Ephraim, made one, and right now in the congregation northern and southern kingdom are back together again.

The classes are not rehearsed, yet the same talking points come out in different places, because the Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to address the prevalent issue of the time, and in the midst of Passover He revealed bitterness throughout the congregations.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” Even while being tried and tempted, the Lord in His faithfulness makes a way out.

What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother. Speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind, and we create a whole other reality that does not even exist in real life. You talk to the brother and you say, damn, all that mess I was thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.

Ephesians 4 says what to put away: “Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.” Bitterness comes first, and the rest come along with it: wrath, anger, clamour, and evil speaking, talking foolish and reckless about the brother, the sister, your wife. That thing has to be put away with extreme hatred. Instead: “be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.” You want to seek pardon from the Lord, but you have hatred toward your brother?

Colossians says what to put on in its place: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” That is how we have to move. The elect of God forbear and forgive one another.

Offenses are going to come in the congregation: a brother says something, a sister says something, and somebody gets offended. We all have to have mercy on one another, because we are all sick. This is a hospital. If a brother coughs on you, you forgive the brother, because everybody in here is sick.

This is how the bitter leaven gets purged. It came up in one congregation where a brother was bitter with his wife and it destroyed a household, and the same spirit showed up elsewhere. Left unchecked, it can destroy a congregation, so we put off the bitterness and put on mercy and forgiveness, as Christ forgave us.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” It is just a part of being in this truth. All of you went through it; you don’t even have to be asked. You caught hell coming into this truth. That is just how it works.

Satan didn’t want to let you go. He didn’t want to give you up. You had family, you had old hoes contacting you from years ago: how did you get my number? Satan. Satan wanted you. He doesn’t want a single one of us to wake up. But we are here.

Is a confrontation with a sister you keep bumping heads with going to take you out? Your marijuana addiction, your addiction to women, your addiction to porn? Or are you going to fight the fight and keep throwing blows back while you are getting hit? As long as you are fighting you are all right; the moment you stop fighting, it is over.

Pressure either bursts pipes or it doesn’t. Pressure exposes the weak points, and then you see where the repairs need to be made. And some go through heavy things, a husband who did this and that, and they are still here, strong as hell. Christ said “It is impossible but that offences will come.” Somebody is going to disappoint you, misunderstand you, correct you, overlook you, frustrate you. You didn’t run away from home over a fight with your sibling; you stayed, and you didn’t stop loving them. We are in the trenches, and we are not leaving. Prepare your soul for it, because the temptation is part of coming to serve the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:4
precepts.why:
Moses chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” What is the sin he refused? John defines it: “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Sin is breaking God’s law. The pleasures of sin are the pleasures of transgressing the law, and if anybody says sin isn’t pleasurable, that’s a lie. It is very fun. But you have to perform abstinence, and choose affliction with the people of God over it, the way Moses did.

That is the difference between Moses and the hireling. A hireling has a temporary time in this truth. He or she doesn’t care about salvation, and is willing to destroy the family, the brotherhood, everything they built up, just for their own sin. The love of sin. The hireling chooses the pleasure of transgressing the law for a season; the true servant chooses to suffer with the people of God.

precepts.label: 2 Thessalonians 2:12
precepts.why:
The pleasures of sin last only “for a season”, and Paul shows where they end: “That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.”

If anybody says sin isn’t pleasurable, that’s a lie; it is very fun. That is exactly why it is dangerous. Those who have pleasure in unrighteousness instead of believing the truth are the ones who are damned. So you have to perform abstinence.

Moses saw it. He chose “rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” The hireling does the opposite. He has a temporary time in this truth and does not care about salvation. He or she is willing to destroy the family, the brotherhood and everything they built up, just for their own sin, for the love of sin. That love of sin is having pleasure in unrighteousness, and its end is damnation.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:8-10
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns of the “root of bitterness springing up”, and John shows what spirit jumps on you when you move that way. “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” That is the history being drawn out from Cain to Esau: the devil sinned from the beginning, and the same spirit runs down through his children.

“For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.” The purpose of Christ is to destroy the works of the devil. So why do we move in the spirit of the devil and think that we are moving in the spirit of Christ?

“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God.” This is the manifestation of the children of God. If you don't do righteousness, you are not of God. The scripture tells us how to deal uprightly with our brother and sister: if there is an offense, go by Matthew 18:15. You don't sow discord and murmur in the midst of the congregation and spread that spirit through our brothers and sisters.

“neither he that loveth not his brother.” When you don't love your brother, you are not moving in the spirit of Christ and you are not counted a child of God. You are the son and daughter of Cain, of Esau. We have to be mindful of this spirit and purge that leaven, that bitter spirit, out of us.

precepts.label: Romans 8:6-7
precepts.why:
Esau was a man of the field and a profane person: his religion is sin. Paul gives the name for that mind: “For to be carnally minded is death.” To be carnally minded is to be Edomite minded, the profane mind. It is death, and that is why he is called the son of perdition.

“but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” When you are spiritually minded, you say, I have to gain my brother. That does not mean we always have to be buddy-buddy, but the scripture says instead of a friend become not an enemy. Brothers turn a brother into an enemy like a rival team in sports, stay pumped up against him and hold on to that feeling, waiting to get back at him. That is the carnal mind. Stay in the spirit.

“Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God.” The Edomite mind, the mind of the spirit of Cain, goes against God and is not subject to his law.

So there are the children of God and the children of the devil, with no in between: either the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The bitter spirit that holds a grudge against a brother is the carnal mind of Esau, and it leads to the same death and rejection he found.

precepts.label: Psalms 50:16-17
precepts.why:
This is the Edomite mindset, the carnal mind at war with God. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Unto the wicked, the white man, God says: hold on, you are carnally minded. Why are you out there talking about in God we trust? Why are you swearing in on the Bible when you do nothing according to the scriptures?

“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” He talks about in God we trust while he has transgenders out there, putting two men together. They don't do anything the scriptures say. They cast the word behind their back, because the carnal mind is at war with God.

This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too. It is the same profane spirit Hebrews names in Esau, whose religion is sin and who despised what was sacred. So we have to make sure we stand in the spirit, and not take God's covenant in our mouth while we cast his words behind us, as a brother does when he holds on to a bitter spirit.

precepts.label: Jude 1:19
precepts.why:
John writes “concerning them that seduce you”, and verse 27 shows how the seduction comes: “ye need not that any man teach you”. The antichrist is going to try to teach you something. He isn't floating in the air going boo; he's teaching. What do you think all these apologetics are? That is the spirit of antichrist. Does that mean the bishops and deacons can't teach us? No. It is the ones who fell away: “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and now all of a sudden they want to teach you.

Jude shows who they are: “These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit.” There will be those who separate themselves, sensual, not having the spirit of the Lord. How can we prove it? What does the Lord require of us on the holy Sabbath day? So when the spirit rises up in you to stay at home, to play Sabbath sick, to forsake the assembling of ourselves together, whose spirit are you moving in? You see how simple that is. The Lord is about unity; he has never been about separation.

When that spirit rises up in you, recognize it, say Satan is trying to get me, and force yourself past that point. Do you wake up every day on the right side of the bed, everything perfect? No, but you push past it. You don't call off work every day. You still go shuffle the white man's papers, stand by the coffee machine and the water cooler and act interested in the job when you don't want to be there. The hope is that once we are among each other, someone who has the spirit of the Lord can be so infectious that it jumps on me, and I get in the spirit of the Lord.

The gripes and unresolved issues, hatred and jealousy, are what Satan uses as a reason to send you back to Caesar Borgia: he spoke rough to me, he didn't say anything to me. Some brothers and sisters, no matter what you do, you can't make them happy; some are ordained to be that sensual brother or sister. That is why we have to stay in the spirit.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 21:27
precepts.why:
John says “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Even the scribes and Pharisees took on the spirit of Cain, of Satan; they moved in the same exact spirit, bitter toward Christ and wanting to put him to death. That spirit will jump on us too, and we have to deal with it. When we are overcome with it, we take on the same attributes Cain did.

“When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” You will have brothers and sisters say, the white man is the devil, they're going to be destroyed, they're going into captivity. And meanwhile you are moving in the same spirit. So you curse Satan, and you curse your own soul, because you have hatred toward your brother. Brothers talk bold against the white man and find themselves in the same spirit as him.

“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.” Whoever is bitter toward his brother is in the spirit of Cain; you are in the same spirit. That hatred is always masked: “Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” He acted like his friend to get him in position.

So we have to exercise ourselves to have a conscience void of offence. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God. Don't allow it to fester and resonate in your spirit until you are overcome, because “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren.”

thread.text: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:18
precepts.why:
Diotrephes is another kind of hireling: he “loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.” And the strange thing is, the apostles set this man up. He was always around and made it appear like he was in the truth. But everybody's problem isn't always sex; some brothers want power, preeminence. I was never anything in the world; I'm going to come in and be somebody. Not by the word of God, but by being deceitful and slick and witty, disrespectful in a secretive way.

Paul settles who has the preeminence: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.” There is only one preeminent, and that is Christ. He is the king; not you, not me. Christ has the preeminence, not Diotrephes. Diotrephes lost his mind, and you know why? He was a hireling.

We have seen it: a brother in the office of ten sees a congregation in Alaska with no senior man, asks no counsel, pops up, and shazam, he's over the congregation, and because he came from the States they love him and accept him. It happened in Ghana and many of the African countries. Another went out, and where were the congregation's donations? In his personal bank account. You can't make this up. These are hirelings; they don't believe, and there is no fear among them.

Diotrephes was “prating against us with malicious words”: always something smart to say, I know what he knows, I know more precepts than you. He would not receive the brethren, not even the ones that taught him, and cast out any who wanted to visit the apostles. But John says “if I come, I will remember his deeds”, and “Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good. He that doeth good is of God: but he that doeth evil hath not seen God.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 62:7
precepts.why:
The four angels hold the four winds “that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree”, and the cry goes out, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” So the question always comes: when are we getting out of here? By right, we want to get out. We pray every day, Lord, bring the destruction so we can leave.

Isaiah 62:7 is that prayer: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” That is what we are doing. We are not to give the Lord rest until he delivers us, establishes us and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.

But the question is, do we really want it? If we really wanted it, there would be no way we would be entertaining sin, no way we would allow evil right up under our noses while telling the Lord to hurry up. You mess around and you get slain.

The Lord has his timetable, and we are not on that level. You only see your own point of view; you do not have the Lord’s vantage point, looking at everything on this planet coming into the synchronicity he is waiting for. The angels are holding back whole armies until the sealing is finished, perhaps until that one last brother wakes up. You cannot push him. What you are responsible for is your own spirit and your own shenanigans. Get yourself right, and he will take care of the rest.

precepts.label: Sirach 36:8
precepts.why:
Here is another thing we say: make the time short, “remember the covenant, and let them declare thy wonderful works.” Lord, make the time short; remember the covenant you made with us; let the nations know you love us, tear these nations up and set us on high.

But you are not on the Lord’s level. Believe me, the Lord will not be a millisecond late when it comes to sending his angels in to destroy our enemies, and you do not know that time. So in our wanting it, what should we be doing? Making sure we are in the right spiritual and mental space, so that when he sends the angels we are not caught off guard as by a thief in the night. We want to declare his wonderful works with a hundred percent confidence, not nervous that we are still in sin somewhere that has not been found out yet.

That is why the Bible says examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith. Congregations have to examine themselves; examine your brothers and your sisters. The people who say, I don’t need to congregate, I can fellowship at home, say it because they don’t want anybody to see their nasty, wicked evil. When you come in here it is going to show, and righteous brothers and sisters are going to point it out.

Accept that correction, because it is love: the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. Somebody telling you where it is at will keep you out of trouble and set you right for when the Lord does send the angels. The angels are holding the four winds until the servants of God are sealed; make sure you are one of them when the time is made short.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:1-5
precepts.why:
Visualize the scene of Revelation 7: four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds. That wind is not the regular wind that blows every day; it is destruction. The four corners are where the militaries are, straining to get at each other, ready to press the buttons, and the angels are holding them back. Bishop Nathanyel, who is an artist, once drew this scene.

2 Esdras 13 is the same scene. “There arose a wind from the sea, that it moved all the waves thereof. And I beheld, and, lo, that man waxed strong with the thousands of heaven: and when he turned his countenance to look, all the things trembled that were seen under him.” That is how Christ is coming back. “And whensoever the voice went out of his mouth, all they burned that heard his voice, like as the earth faileth when it feeleth the fire.” If Christ is coming back with that kind of power, you think he will not see your wicked thoughts and the things you thought you were hiding? You don’t want to be on the wrong side of that magnificent coming.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. The armies are setting up to fight against our deliverer. These nations do not want Christ to save us; they want us to remain in sin and evil so they can keep subduing and destroying the Israelites.

So the Lord tells the four angels, hold the four winds; don’t let them fight yet. When Christ comes back these armies will try to fight him to keep us in slavery, and he is coming to destroy every last one of them. And if we are not right, he is going to destroy us too. Brothers and sisters, make sure your diligence is on par.

precepts.label: Luke 20:20
precepts.why:
“Think not upon those that have walked feignedly before thee.” To feign means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. And Luke shows feigning in action: “And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words.” They pretended to be just men so they could catch Christ in his words.

During the time of Christ there were a lot of fake brothers among them, so we expect that to be true today. There is going to be an explosion, a spiritual explosion, an influx of believers, especially from the Christian church: 3,000 one day, 5,000 another day. It's going to happen, because the scriptures say it.

But we have to be mindful: there will be feigned people among them. Ezra asks God not to think upon those, “but remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

precepts.label: Luke 9:62
precepts.why:
“And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” That's a hireling: he put his hand to the work and then looked back. Some of y'all are sitting here right now. There is a God; remember that.

This is where you self-examine. Am I being a phony, a hypocrite among the brethren? Am I walking feignedly? Only you can answer that. You and God know the answer; we don't.

Ezra prays that God would think not upon those that walked feignedly, but remember them that have known his fear. The one who looks back from the plough is not fit for the kingdom.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:38
precepts.why:
“Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.” That was the guy who put the talent in the napkin: he drew back.

As we're doing the restructuring, certain captains get asked, why did you move this brother from this position to that position? Oh, he's not the same any more. When he came in, he was on fire; we didn't have to tell him what to do. Now you've got to yell at him, you've got to force him. So drop him down and move him to the side, like we read in 1 Corinthians 6 today.

The Lord has no pleasure in the one who draws back. That is walking feignedly before him, and Ezra asks God to think not upon those, but to remember them that according to his will have known his fear.

precepts.label: Psalms 44:18
precepts.why:
Against the hireling who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, and the man who draws back, stands Israel's confession: “Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way.” That's how you've got to be. That's how we have to be.

The heart that does not turn back and the steps that do not decline are what it means to walk before God unfeignedly. Those are the ones Ezra asks God to remember: “remember them, which according to thy will have known thy fear.”

So examine yourself. Has your heart turned back? Have your steps declined from his way since you first came in on fire? You and God know the answer.

precepts.label: Luke 24:32
precepts.why:
“And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?” When those scriptures come out, your heart is supposed to be burning for this.

How do I get this word out? What ideas do I have? I want to give my time to this truth; everything else outside of this doesn't matter. If your heart is not burning with the word of God, if you don't have the desire to learn, to teach, to better yourself, to better the nation of Israel, you are going to fade away. You're a hireling.

You could be in 5 years, 10 years, 20 years, but this word is supposed to make your heart burn to get it out. The hireling walks feignedly; the one whose heart burns is the one who has known God's fear.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:5
precepts.why:
Feign is a verb that means to pretend, to fake, to give a false show of something. It includes pretending an illness: a lot of sisters get Sabbath sick. It includes faking an emotion, or making up an excuse. Remember the brother who used to go around teaching fake it till you make it? Don't raise that man up; he isn't right. To feign means to pretend: you are a fake brother, you are pretending.

Paul sets the opposite: “Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned.” Unfeigned faith: not feigned, not folly.

The whole end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart and a faith that is not pretended. That is the walk Ezra asks God to remember, and the feigned walk is the one he asks God to think not upon.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:22
precepts.why:
“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently.” Unfeigned: don't be fake, don't be phony.

Some brothers can fake it real good. If a sister asks us, what about this brother, we can only tell her what you show us. Is he really like that? She's got to talk to him more in depth, more personally, to find out how he truly is.

That is why the love of the brethren has to be unfeigned, out of a pure heart. Only you and God know whether you are walking feignedly; we only see what you show us.

precepts.label: Romans 12:10-11
precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” That is the unfeigned love of the brethren, real and not put on.

“Not slothful in business”: not lazy concerning God's work. “fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit. “serving the Lord.”

This is the opposite of walking feignedly. The feigned brother came in on fire and now has to be yelled at and forced; the hireling looked back from the plough. The one Ezra asks God to remember, one “which according to thy will have known thy fear”, is kindly affectioned to the brethren, not slothful in God's business, and on fire in spirit, serving the Lord.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.label: Jeremiah 1:5
precepts.why:
Ezra says every one that shall be saved, and shall escape by his works, by keeping the commandments, and by faith in what is written, “Shall be preserved from the said perils, and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.” That is when the kingdom is set up. And why does he say he sanctified them from the beginning? Jeremiah shows it.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Where did he know us? In spirit. This is a physical domain, but he knew us in the spirit world, in another dimension. He did something to our spirit before our parents had relations to bring us forth. You are here because of a conversation God had with you before you even came into this world.

So you people are here because God cares about you. You are not here by accident. There is something in your spirit that God said, I need to fix you, so that when the time comes to destroy the earth, you come back to me and are not in your pride.

The third of Israelites were sanctified from the beginning, from the foundation of the earth. He said, these spirits I am going to love, and these spirits I am going to reject and destroy. God is good all the time to the people that keep his commandments. To you people breaking God’s laws, he is not good. So do not listen to anybody saying God is good all the time; that is not scriptural.

That is why the rest of the chapter is so hard: those who abused his ways, loathed his law while they had liberty and despised the place of repentance “must know it after death by pain.” The sanctified are preserved; the proud are not.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:1
precepts.why:
Ezra says, “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed.” Before the world was made there was a council, and no one spoke against what was ordained. Christ said, these spirits over here, y’all are the twelve tribes of Israel; those spirits right there, y’all are the Jebusites. No one disagreed. When you are before the creator you are not going to say, no, I don’t want to be the Edomites.

It is like a screenplay writer and a director. You show up as the actor, they give you the script, and you say, this is a good movie, who am I going to play? Michael B. Jordan agreed to play Killmonger; they portrayed him as the bad guy, but Killmonger is actually the good guy. Chadwick Boseman agreed to his role. Everybody agreed to their role, then the movie was made and we cheered, Wakanda forever. The same way the Lord sat in his council and everyone was given their roles and tasks.

Wisdom of Solomon proves he knew beforehand: “As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do.” The chapter before goes into the destruction of Egypt and all the plagues that came. What is very telling is that he did not show mercy in his wrath, because he already knew what they were going to do.

So what Paul said and Peter said, the prophet Ezra says the same: it was ordained before the world was made. Now “the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”, and the Lord already knew who would be ungodly and dealt with them accordingly.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 1:5
precepts.why:
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” How can the Lord know how we are all going to move? Because it is already ordained, from the council Ezra speaks of, when he prepared the world “which was not yet made” and “no man spake against me.”

Think about it. As Jeremiah is running around as a little kid playing with other little kids, the Lord says, when you grow up, you are going to be a mighty prophet in the earth.

The same way with these young men. If I could go back and be ten, eleven, twelve years old learning this truth! But learning it when you did is ordained of the Lord. If you were ten, eleven, twelve back in the day, you may not have withstood the trials that came to many brothers and sisters then, when YouTube was not as big as it is now. There was not every topic and every class online for you to watch and say, let me get my spirit right. When I was ten or eleven and a trial came, would I have withstood? Only the Lord knows. The Lord said, I will call you when I need you.

That is every single one of us. It is ordained by the Lord for you young ones to be here in 2026, when your parents can send you a class for the spirit you are dealing with, so you are able to abide in this time. Many fell out back then. You were known and set apart before you came out of the womb, called at the time the Lord chose.

When you look across the room, you are not wondering if she can help with your resume. You are thinking about the curves, the lips, the perfume. Sirach says: “Wisdom lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and maketh him to sit among great men.” Whatever the brother’s finances, even if he is just starting at the bottom of a job, none of that matters. Wisdom lifts up his head and sets him among great men.

Don’t raise your hand. And don’t let social media fool you: every woman wants a man. A woman who says she doesn’t need one is going against nature. Her body releases hormones when she is under her husband; that is why she falls asleep ten minutes into the movie she asked you to watch. All her fear goes out the window, because she is safe.

She is bone of his bone, flesh of his flesh, made in the man’s image, and she is his glory. That is why little girls look like their daddy: her body is the portal that brings us into this life, but the seed comes from the man. precepts.label: Ephesians 2:11
precepts.why:
In the days of the Maccabees, “many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” They consented to the religion of the Greeks, idolatry: they gave up what God told them to do and said, we are going to do what they want us to do. That is Hellenization. They profaned the sabbath and left the feast days, sacrificed swine's flesh and unclean beasts, left their children uncircumcised, and made their souls abominable, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.”

Paul reminds the Ephesians of exactly that: “Wherefore remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands”. Remember, back in the day, you were Gentiles. What is another word for Gentile? Hellenized Jews, Greeks.

Why were they called Uncircumcision? Because it was their fathers, back in the time of the Maccabees, who decided they were not going to circumcise their children. The Circumcision in the flesh were those whose fathers decided to stay, who did not give up, who did not allow their children to become Hellenized. Paul is telling them, remember: you were living like heathens. To the Corinthians he says the same: “ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.”

The racial slur this country put on our people is another form of that same Hellenization. The devil called us that. It is one of the most hateful epithets in the English language, and we took it up, changed the ending, and called it friendly and empowering. There is nothing empowering about it. Your oppressor named you that to demean you; you did not call yourself that. If you call someone that, you are telling them they are unrepentant, that they have fully learned the customs of the heathen, and that the Hellenization worked.

That was Esau's mission: to take away our heritage and make us something we are not, so that we forget the law. Brothers and sisters, we are not that word. We never have been, and Lord's will, we will never be again. When we come out of that mind frame, we do not refer to each other that way.
